# Composing with the curated components

Distilled from the source repo's `web-store-components` skill — the parts that apply to composing a page from existing components, not to authoring new ones.

## Read the props, don't guess them

Every curated component's real prop names, variants, and states are in `catalog.json`. Read a component's entry there before using it — don't guess a prop name from a similar component elsewhere; prop surfaces are deliberately not uniform.

## Layout building blocks

`Grid` + `Span` is the layout system every real page section uses:

```vue
<Grid>
  <Span size="content">
    <!-- your section -->
  </Span>
</Grid>
```

`Span` sizes: `content` (centred, capped width — most sections), `fluid`/`full` (edge-to-edge), `carousel` (full-bleed on narrow, centred on wide). Use `Span`, not raw `max-width`/`margin: 0 auto`, so your page's responsive behavior matches every other page in this design system.

### Source: `web-store-components` — "Pattern 4 — Graceful-absent (nullable) props & assets"

Design **"absent" as a first-class state**. A `null` asset or `null` label collapses the element
rather than erroring or rendering a placeholder.

```vue
<span v-if="label" class="…">{{ label }}</span>           <!-- null ⇒ no label -->
<img  v-if="assets.brand.mpColourIcon" :src="assets.brand.mpColourIcon" alt="MP" />  <!-- null ⇒ no icon -->
```
A store that lacks a feature simply sets the asset/string to `null` (see `loyaltyIcon`,
`mpColourIcon`, `account.playerCardLabel`) — no component edit.

---

### Source: `web-store-components` — "Pattern 5 — Single source of truth (one component per concept)"

There is **one** component per identity concept, reused everywhere it appears. Do **not**
inline-duplicate its markup — divergent copies are exactly the inconsistency this rule prevents.

- Player identity → `PlayerCard.vue` everywhere (account popover, guest-lookup result, page sign-in
  section, any future checkout confirmation). Props flex it per context/store; the markup lives once.
- If you need the same visual in a new place, **import the component** and pass props — never
  paste its template.
